clue.text: Scope for the firm with a thousand to spend

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
to pass time is to spend it

explanation.surface: A company sets aside a thousand to spend on a project's range.
explanation.definitionFit: Range or extent, as in the breadth of a subject, is a synonym of scope.

clue.text: A drawing instrument

parts.note: reads like a draughtsman's pencil or compass, but the drawing meant is pulling stoppers from wine bottles

explanation.definitionFit: The tool draws out a cork from a bottle, so it is literally an instrument for drawing.

clue.text: Doesn't speak well of a Welsh place

definitions.meaning: a headland and village on Swansea Bay in south Wales

explanation.surface: Someone is slow to praise a town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk unclearly is to murmur indistinctly; the same word names a seaside district near Swansea.

clue.text: Making one bad and vicious

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are used to make something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Doing something makes a person bad and cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' tells you to make a new word from ONE, BAD and AND, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Depraved, wholly given up to vice, is the old sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Lay off the wine!

definitions.meaning: an old name for dry white wine from Spain or the Canaries, as in Falstaff's favourite drink

explanation.surface: A plea to a drinker to give up the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss someone from employment is to fire them; the same word is a Shakespearean term for sherry.

clue.text: Still manufacturing sausage

indicators.note: making something out of these letters signals a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: A butcher is still at work making sausages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb meaning 'yet', but it is a verb meaning to calm.
explanation.definitionFit: To calm or soothe a pain or a feeling is to ease it, a synonym.

clue.text: Head of department under notice: apply here!

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written under another comes after it

parts.note: an AD is a notice advertising something
a government minister heads a ministry or department

explanation.surface: A job advertisement for a departmental head invites applications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apply here!' reads like the end of a job notice; the definition is 'apply', as in applying a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To give or dispense medicine or justice is to apply it.

clue.text: A series of notes on fish

definitions.meaning: a musical sequence of notes ascending or descending
the small plates found on a fish's skin

explanation.surface: Someone jots down a series of notes about fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A run of musical notes like do-re-mi is one sense; a thin plate covering a fish's body is the other.

clue.text: Rising girl model, for the fuller figure?

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Ida is a girl's name
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: A rising young model caters for larger sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatty, relating to body fat, describes the fuller figure.

clue.text: Silver taken in before becoming a bore

indicators.note: one word is taken in by another, so it goes inside

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone accepts silver before becoming a tedious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bore' seems to be a dull person; it is a tidal wave surging up a river, such as the Severn bore.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal surge up an estuary is called a bore; this is another name for it.

clue.text: Dance music that's strange to half the band

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

indicators.note: only the front half of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Dance music that half the band find weird.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance and the music written for it.

clue.text: Opposing the formation of a club in future

indicators.note: the club goes in the word for future

parts.note: coming, as in the coming year, means future
a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: Resistance to setting up a club in the years ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting against something is a synonym of opposing it.

clue.text: A light helmet with bearing on green stuff

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece on another follows it

parts.note: salad is leafy green food
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A helmet worn while carrying some greens.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a medieval light helmet, also spelt sallet.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifteenth-century open helmet, often with a neck guard, of light construction.

clue.text: Foreigner held back by prior to see a beast

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, prior to

indicators.note: the word for foreigner is turned to read back to front

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland, a foreigner to the British

explanation.surface: An alien is kept behind so as to watch an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A horned grazing animal of Africa and Asia is an example of a beast.

clue.text: Contest an illustrator's racket

parts.note: a battle is a contest
Gustave Doré was a famous French illustrator

explanation.surface: An artist's noisy dispute is a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' seems to mean a din; it is the bat for an old game, the forerunner of badminton.
explanation.definitionFit: The light bat used with a shuttlecock in the old game is a kind of racket.

clue.text: Having got up in a bad temper — is enraged

indicators.note: the answer lies in the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Someone gets out of bed in a foul mood, furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Stood up or got out of bed is the past participle of the verb to rise.

clue.text: Odd to see as bent those not turning up

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: It looks strange to call the no-shows crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' tells you to rearrange SEE, AS and BENT.
explanation.definitionFit: People who stay away from school or work when expected are no-shows.

clue.text: Tourist area with points in favour of dividing the home

indicators.note: the pieces split the home word into two parts

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home
E and W are compass points
for means in favour of

explanation.surface: A holiday region where the home team scores points.
explanation.definitionFit: A national park in Hampshire, England, it is a popular visitor destination.

clue.text: Balance is hard on a road

parts.note: steely means hard as steel

explanation.surface: Keeping one's equilibrium is tough on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An old weighing device with a sliding weight on a long arm is a type of balance.

clue.text: Fowl and duck races in river setting

indicators.note: the river forms a setting round the other pieces

parts.note: the Wye is a river in Wales and England
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O
TT is the Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: Chickens and ducks race along a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An American breed of domestic chicken is a kind of fowl.

clue.text: One who works like fury to exact satisfaction

definitions.text: One who works like fury to exact satisfaction

parts.words: One who works like fury to exact satisfaction
parts.note: suggests someone working very hard, but the Furies of myth punished wrongdoers to exact revenge

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes revenge for a wrong exacts satisfaction, as the mythical Furies did.

clue.text: Something this nurse's absence may disclose, said Belloc

definitions.text: Something this nurse's absence may disclose, said Belloc

parts.words: Something this nurse's absence may disclose, said Belloc
parts.note: recalls Belloc's cautionary tale of Jim, told to keep hold of Nurse for fear of finding something more dreadful

explanation.walkthrough: Hilaire Belloc's poem 'Jim' ends: 'And always keep a-hold of Nurse / For fear of finding something worse.' The word also hides in 'nurse' minus its N, but the clue rests on the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Belloc's moral warns that leaving one's nurse may lead to finding something more unpleasant.

clue.text: Soundly knocked three armies right back

indicators.note: the armies' letters are read back to front

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, taken three times

explanation.surface: Three armies get properly thrashed and pushed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses TATATA to give ATATAT, after R.
explanation.definitionFit: The word imitates the sound of repeated knocking on a door.

clue.text: Made a fuss about name notched on the edge

indicators.note: the fuss word goes round the other piece

parts.note: created, as in 'created a scene', means made a fuss

explanation.surface: Someone complained about a name being scratched on a border.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a scalloped or toothed margin, as on some leaves, is a botanical term for notched.

clue.text: Troubles do exist in the Civil Service

indicators.note: the existence word goes in the abbreviation

parts.note: CS is the abbreviation for the Civil Service
are means do exist

explanation.surface: Problems really are found in government departments.
explanation.definitionFit: Worries or anxieties are synonyms of troubles.

clue.text: Commercial articles in Turkey

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
AN and A are indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Trade goods sold in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in southern Turkey, so a place found within that country.

clue.text: Being implacable

definitions.meaning: a human creature, as in 'a mere human'
deadly, unforgiving, as in a deadly enemy

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot be appeased.
explanation.definitionFit: A human being subject to death is one sense; a deadly, unrelenting enemy is the other.

clue.text: He gave to Mis'ry all he had, a …" Gray (Elegy)

definitions.text: He gave to Mis'ry all he had, a …" Gray (Elegy)

parts.words: He gave to Mis'ry all he had, a …" Gray (Elegy)
parts.note: a line from Thomas Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard, with its last word left for the solver to supply

explanation.walkthrough: The Epitaph of Gray's Elegy reads: 'He gave to Mis'ry all he had, a tear, / He gain'd from Heav'n ('twas all he wish'd) a friend.'
explanation.definitionFit: The poor youth of the poem had nothing to give misery but a drop of weeping.

clue.text: Long-winded discourse is more a girl's fault

indicators.note: a fault puts the letters wrong, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Rambling talk is more a girl's failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fault' tells you to rearrange MORE, A and GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambling, convoluted account is a long-winded piece of talk.

clue.text: Unusually wide, for example

definitions.meaning: in cricket a wide is one kind of run not off the bat

explanation.surface: Something unusually broad, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide, a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach, earns a run added to the score but not off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Exceptionally, beyond the usual, is one sense; in cricket, a bonus run like a wide or bye is the other.

clue.text: Champion rider at the seaside makes an appearance

parts.note: surf, the breaking waves that a beach rider rides on
an ace is a champion, an expert

explanation.surface: A star surfer on the beach puts in an appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: The outward look of something, its exterior, is its outward appearance.

clue.text: Turned to trade perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A business shifted to commerce, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange TO and TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun round on an axis, revolved, is a synonym of turned.
